h: מוֹצָאֵי יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, ו׳ Motzei Yom Kippur, 6

p: We have already spoken of this,
that the purpose of the Melaveh Malkah meal
is to draw the holiness of Shabbos
only in the holiness of Shabbos,
which is not so with the other festivals,
to the aspect of drawing holiness afterward;
for if one wished, on the day after,
to sanctify it by eating matzah
he would accomplish nothing by this.
the time of the giving of our Torah:
is there the indwelling of the giving of the Written Torah;
וַהֲגַם שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סִפְרֵי עֵקֶב, פִּסְקָא נח)
"Every day they should be in your eyes as new,"
for that is the power of renewal
in each one according to the aspect of his soul.
of the giving of the Written Torah
הוּא רַק בְּאוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם שֶׁל מַתַּן תּוֹרָה
is only on that day of Matan Torah,
and it lacks the power to draw holiness
except for the bestowal of the aspect of the holiness of Shabbos,
שֶׁהוּא מֵעֵין הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא (בְּרָכוֹת נז, ב)
which is a semblance of Olam HaBa (Berachos 57b):
it has the power to be drawn
as we find with great souls,
to whom Hashem Yisbarach gave a taste all their days
of a semblance of Olam HaBa,
כְּמַאֲמַר חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא יז, א)
And similar to what they said (Berachos 17a):
"May you see your world in your lifetime" —
of the fruit of his deeds that awaits in Olam HaBa
And this comes from the power of the holiness of Shabbos,
וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה
"And God saw all that He had made,
and behold, it was very good,"
meaning that all matters in the world
are rectified into the aspect of good.
And all the more so now,
when there coincides with Motzei Shabbos
which is also an aspect of the holiness of Shabbos
by virtue of the mikra'ei kodesh,
which come from the arousal from below,
on the past Motzei Shabbos Kodesh —
certainly there is an indwelling of holiness
For on any other Shabbos day
there is only a drawing of holiness
from the aspect of the Shabbos day itself,
in that on the day itself
it merely becomes known regarding all matters
the matter returns to its former state;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן אַחַר יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
there is specifically an indwelling of holiness
שֶׁכָּל מַה שֶּׁהָיָה עָבַר עַד כֹּה
since all that had passed until now
and "from here on begins the reckoning";
consequently there is an indwelling of joy
in this mitzvah meal in its own right,
and not merely by way of drawing,
and drink your wine with a good heart,
כִּי כְבָר רָצָה הָאֱלֹהִים אֶת מַעֲשֶׂיךָ
for God has already accepted your deeds" —
meaning that from this there is now born
the joy and the good heart,
all the deeds, every one of them,
and they have all been turned to good.
Now, it says in the Gemara (Arachin 11a)
תַּחַת אֲשֶׁר לֹא עָבַדְתָּ אֶת ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ
"Because you did not serve Hashem your God
with joy and with goodness of heart, amid abundance of everything":
that is with joy and goodness of heart?
You must say, this is song."
'The precepts of Hashem are upright, gladdening the heart.'"
And this is what Tosafos there labored over
that there is in the Midrash
that he had occupied himself with Torah —
it is called tov lev, "good of heart,"
And this is because tov levav
means that there have been turned and brought into accord
כְּעִנְיַן אֲמָרָם זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת נד, א)
וְאָהַבְתָּ אֵת ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ
"'And you shall love Hashem your God with all your heart (levavecha)' —
"the heart of the wise is at his right,
and the heart of the fool at his left" (Koheles 10:2),
and that one too is turned to good.
meaning that through words of Torah
that the wise heart at his right is strengthened
so that he not be lured after the foolish heart,
כְּעִנְיַן אֲמָרָם זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סוּכָּה נב, ב)
drag him to the beis midrash;
if he is stone, he dissolves."
וְעִם כָּל זֶה אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שָׁם)
and were it not that Hakadosh Baruch Hu helps him,
because the yetzer hara is still present
only it is subdued for the time being.
But regarding a mitzvah meal it says,
and drink your wine with a good heart,"
שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז גַּם כֵּן עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
which also alludes to words of Torah,
And so it is in the holy Zohar,
פָּרָשַׁת עֵקֶב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רעא, ב)
the bread of the Written Torah
and the wine of the Oral Torah.)
And this is the aspect of the Written Torah,
while "drink of the wine I have mixed"
which specifically is likened to wine and water,
which flow down from a high place
And about this specifically it says,
כִּי זֶהוּ פְּעוּלַּת עֵסֶק תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
for this is the effect of engaging in the Oral Torah:
to strengthen the wise heart at his right,
so as not to be lured after the foolish heart,
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סוּכָּה נב, ב)
in the wording, "If this repulsive one meets you,
drag him to the beis midrash" specifically,
which is the study hall of the Sages,
which alludes to the Oral Torah,
